bullets.title: NVDA: Considers reducing HBM in Rubin Ultra GPU due to shortage; also seeking 6G AI-RAN suppliers in China
bullets.body: The Information reports NVIDIA is weighing a design change to reduce high-bandwidth memory content in its upcoming Rubin Ultra GPU amid a shortage of advanced HBM chips. Separately, NVIDIA is urgently seeking Chinese AI base station suppliers for 6G AI-RAN development. Neither development appears bullish for HBM suppliers in the near term.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK: Memory stocks under pressure; Terafab DRAM threat, Jefferies slashes SNDK PT 42%
bullets.body: Jefferies cut its Sandisk (SNDK) price target from $3,000 to $1,750 (a 42% reduction) while maintaining Buy, citing reset expectations. Separately, Tesla's Terafab is hiring memory process engineers signaling a potential long-term competitive threat to the DRAM oligopoly (MU, Samsung, SK Hynix). MU showed the strongest bullish options flow on the day despite mixed sentiment; one trader flagged DRAM as a potential net short/underweight.

bullets.title: WDC/SNDK sharp declines: WDC -21%, SNDK -13% intraday
bullets.body: Western Digital fell 21% and SanDisk dropped 13% in today's session, consistent with broader memory sector weakness tied to NVIDIA's potential HBM reduction plans and South Korean memory names (SK Hynix -10.4%, Samsung -6.3%) also collapsing.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $25B bond offering draws $115B demand; AI expansion funding
bullets.body: Alphabet launched a $25 billion multi-tranche investment-grade bond offering (maturities 2–40 years) that drew approximately $115 billion in investor demand, causing hyperscaler bond spreads to widen. This follows prior debt raises of $30B+ in February and $25B in November; the company is funding capex entirely through debt issuance. AMZN raised a similar amount one month prior.

bullets.title: TSLA: Terafab confirmed in Grimes County TX; targets 1+ terawatt compute/year; Musk allocates ~25% to Optimus
bullets.body: Tesla confirmed Terafab will be built in Grimes County, Texas, targeting over 1 terawatt of annual AI compute production. Musk estimates roughly 25% of Terafab compute output will go to Tesla Optimus robotics and ~75% to AI/spacecraft. Tesla also posted job openings for memory process engineers, with Musk prioritizing DRAM production.

bullets.title: MSFT: Only Mag 7 name with positive FCF; OpenAI = ~70% of AI revenue; 4th India data center live
bullets.body: Microsoft was cited as the only major tech company currently generating positive free cash flow. OpenAI accounts for roughly 70% of Microsoft's AI revenue, highlighting partnership concentration risk. Microsoft also launched its fourth AI data center region in India as part of a $20.5 billion country investment.

bullets.title: ANET: Arista reports earnings (record Foxconn/Wistron results noted in same update)
bullets.body: Arista Networks posted earnings during the session per daily semiconductor/networking update. The same update also noted Foxconn and Wistron posting record results and Celestica completing a $3 billion capital raise, suggesting strong data center supply chain momentum.

bullets.title: MTSI: Blowout Q4 guide — adj. EPS $1.97-$2.03 vs. $1.48 consensus; revenue $415-$425M
bullets.body: Macom Technology guided Q4 adjusted EPS to $1.97–$2.03, well above the $1.48 consensus estimate, with revenue guided to $415–$425 million. This is a significant beat-and-raise that should attract attention given the photonics/RF infrastructure theme.

bullets.title: AXTI/LITE: Lumentum CEO calls InP shortage 'severe and worsening,' exceeding DRAM/NAND constraints
bullets.body: Lumentum's CEO characterized the Indium Phosphide shortage as severe, worsening, and now exceeding constraints in DRAM and NAND. AXTI recently signed a partnership with LITE (Lumentum), providing direct supply-side exposure. Separately, a NOK InP supply issue appears localized to manufacturing/testing bottlenecks rather than broad optics shortage, per PhotonCap analysis.

bullets.title: Semiconductor test cycle inflecting: Advantest raises 2026 memory TAM +12%, SoC TAM +21%; OSAT capex at ATH
bullets.body: Advantest revised 2026 memory test TAM to $2.75B (from $2.45B, +12%) and SoC TAM to $11B (from $9.1B, +21%). Q2 test capex at major OSATs reached an all-time high at nearly 2x prior peak, with monthly tester installs also at a record. Teradyne noted test equipment is now growing faster than fab equipment for the first time in a decade, with memory book-to-bill >2.

bullets.title: VIAV: Solid earnings; data center revenue doubles YoY, now 40% of total revenue
bullets.body: Viavi Solutions beat on revenue, margins, and EPS. Data center revenue more than doubled year-over-year organically (excluding Spirent) and now represents roughly 40% of total company revenue, signaling a structural mix shift.

bullets.title: CEG: Raises full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $11.50-$12.50, above $11.70 consensus
bullets.body: Constellation Energy boosted its adjusted operating EPS forecast to $11.50–$12.50 from the prior range of $11–$12, coming in above the Bloomberg consensus of $11.70. Q2 operating revenue was reported at $7.50 billion.

bullets.title: AAOI: Pre-earnings setup — Q2 bridge quarter at ~$190M; Q3 guide of $300-320M needed for $1.1B annual target
bullets.body: Pre-earnings analysis flags Q2 as a bridge quarter with base case ~$190M revenue and 29.5% gross margin. The key inflection is Q3 guidance: below $270M would be concerning absent explanation, while $300–$320M is needed to support the $1.1 billion annual revenue target.

bullets.title: PLTR: Analyst argues shorting down 20% while fundamentals improve is poor risk/reward
bullets.body: Commentary suggests PLTR's fundamentals are improving, not deteriorating, making the short thesis after a 20% drawdown unattractive. The stock was previously a crowded long at peak valuation; current setup may favor longs after the reset.

bullets.title: CIEN: WaveLogic 6 Extreme can encrypt 1.6 Tb/s traffic using QKD-generated keys at wire speed
bullets.body: Ciena's WaveLogic 6 Extreme platform can encrypt 1.6 terabits per second of conventional traffic at wire speed using quantum key distribution-generated keys — a differentiated quantum-safe encryption capability that positions CIEN for next-generation secure networking.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Merger deadline June 4, 2027; California AG litigation strategy could run out the clock
bullets.body: LightShed analysts note Paramount could win on legal merits but still lose the Warner Bros. Discovery merger deal if the California AG's clock-running litigation strategy extends past the June 4, 2027 pivotal date. The CA AG does not need to win in court — just delay.

bullets.title: CMCSA/NFLX: LightShed analysts debate Peacock leapfrogging to #2 streamer position by 2027
bullets.body: LightShed analysts are evaluating whether Peacock (Comcast) can reach the #2 streaming platform position behind Netflix by 2027, suggesting meaningful subscriber growth expectations for the service.

bullets.title: OKLO: SMR achieves nuclear criticality — key development milestone
bullets.body: Oklo's small modular reactor reached criticality, achieving a self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction, a major milestone supporting U.S. advanced nuclear technology development and Oklo's commercial pathway.

bullets.title: Mag 7 premarket snapshot: AAPL +1.1%, AMZN +0.7%, META +0.5%, GOOGL +0.5%, NVDA +0.6%, TSLA flat, MSFT -0.6%
bullets.body: Premarket moves showed Mag 7 broadly higher, partially offsetting weakness in chip and memory names. Apple led with +1.1%, while Microsoft was the sole decliner at -0.6%.

bullets.title: ARM/MRVL/MU: Trader adds on tech dip; ARM cited as 'biggest winner ever' since IPO
bullets.body: One active trader reported adding to ARM, MRVL, and MU positions last week and earlier this week, using a rule of buying favorite tech names when QQQ or XLK dips 10%. Separately, another poster cited ARM as their single largest winner ever since post-IPO entry.
